resources.string: The network changed - restarting the server on %1$s
Install downloads Node.js, git and VirtualTabletop. It needs an internet connection once - after that the server runs offline.
Only %1$s of storage are free on this phone. The installation takes about %2$s, so it may well run out of space - free some room first.
Start the server and open the room on any device in the same network.
Node.js takes a few seconds to come up on a phone.
%1$s\n\nPress %2$s again to carry on where it stopped.
Open the room in the browser
The server stops and everyone playing is disconnected. The rooms are saved and are still there next time.
The download stops where it is. Nothing that arrived is lost - pressing the button again later carries on from there.

Just want to play? Open virtualtabletop.io in a browser - that is the game itself, always up to date, and it needs no app at all.

This app is for playing with no internet around. It runs the VirtualTabletop server on this phone, so the phone, a tablet and a laptop on the same WiFi - or on this phone's hotspot - can play together on a train, in a garden or anywhere else offline.

Install fetches Node.js, git and VirtualTabletop once. That needs a connection and about %1$s of storage, and everything it does is printed here. It can be pressed again to carry on if the connection breaks. Start server then hands out the address the other devices open.

Thank you to the Termux project (termux.dev): Node.js and git for Android are their work, built and kept up to date by them, and this app simply installs their packages.
